description:
Across the dusty plains of the Moon and the crimson deserts of Mars lie the silent relics of human ingenuity—lander bases, inactive rovers, and scientific instruments. Far from being mere discarded equipment, these objects represent the pioneering monuments of space exploration.
​Team AstroHUB transforms NASA's open spatial data into an immersive digital storytelling experience.
summary:
What We Developed:
We created a bilingual educational framework for children aged 8–13 that reframes retired space hardware—such as Apollo 15’s Falcon module and the Mars Ingenuity helicopter—not as space debris, but as "sleeping historical explorers." By combining official NASA data with creative anthropomorphic storytelling, we turn complex technical milestones into engaging, character-driven narratives.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
Traditional space education often relies on dry data, leaving young learners disconnected from deep-space history. Our project bridges this gap by blending scientific rigor with emotional engagement. Through first-person perspectives where the hardware itself "speaks," engineering concepts and early space archaeology become accessible and memorable.

Why It Matters:
This initiative introduces space heritage conservation to young minds. By teaching children to value the silent monuments left on the Moon and Mars, we foster empathy and inspire the next generation of explorers to view space not just as a race forward, but as a shared human legacy.
details:
What does your project do, and how does it work?

"The Star-Sleepers" is a digital storybook project developed to inspire a love for space and science in children aged 8–13. The project features real space mission icons—such as Apollo 15’s lunar module "Falcon" and the Mars helicopter "Ingenuity"—speaking in the first person. Instead of using a technical and dry tone, it brings these machines to life through a cinematic narrative, highlighting their emotions, solitude, and cosmic guardianship, taking children on an engaging time-travel adventure.

What are the benefits, and what is the intended impact?

  • Passion for Space and Science: Instead of fostering an abstract interest, it helps children build an emotional connection with astronomy and space history through the eyes of the machines.
  • Engaging Learning: By offering an adventurous and age-appropriate storyline, it supports reading habits and makes learning fun.
  • Historical and Scientific Awareness: It seamlessly weaves in real NASA data (such as Falcon's collected rocks, Ingenuity's 72 flights, or the fabric piece from the Wright brothers' plane) far away from boring textbook formats.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Visual and Design Tools: AI-powered image generation tools and the Canva platform were used to give the project a professional graphic-novel aesthetic, avoiding childish drawings.
  • Text and Narrative Infrastructure: Cinematic storytelling techniques, digital flipbook formats, and structured page layouts were utilized to shape the narrative voice.

How creative is your project, and what factors did your team consider? Our project is highly creative as it blends unique concepts like "space archaeology" and "cosmic guardianship" instead of relying on standard space documentaries or encyclopedias. Our team considered the following critical factors during the process:

  • Personalization and Emotion: By using an anthropomorphic approach (attributing human-like qualities to scientific objects), we evoked empathy, curiosity, and excitement in the readers.
  • Nostalgic and Romantic Tone: Instead of a dry, academic delivery, we chose a cinematic, fairytale-like tone that nurtures children's imagination.
  • Visual-Text Harmony: To keep children's attention alive and prevent them from getting distracted, every section is supported by high-quality, cool, and aesthetic graphic novel illustrations.
